mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that typically precedes economic slowdowns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0, or the Rank IC over 2 years is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy faces a demand shock.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0), supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output signal an impending recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in economic contraction.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0, or the Rank IC over 2 years is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) series indicates strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, which consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates higher corporate earnings from the housing sector.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC over 1 year is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to predict positive returns: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) fall below 400,000 million dollars, it indicates a sharp drop in consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate revenue.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS < 400000, or the Rank IC over 1 year is below 0.01.
